names.note: Read out of doxologia.ro's line for 9 februarie.
Read out of saint.gr's line for 9 Φεβρουαρίου, «Άγιοι Μάρκελλος επίσκοπος Σικελίας, Φιλάγριος επίσκοπος Κύπρου και Παγκράτιος επίσκοπος Ταυρομενίου», with the rank word and the see left off.

Read out of the Охридски пролог’s heading for 9. јул ст. ст., „Свешт. муч. Панкратије еп. Тавроменијски“ — „Свешт. муч.“ is one rank and „еп.“ the other, both of which `types` already carries, and „Тавроменијски“ is the see that second rank governs and comes off with it, as „Критски“, „Московски“, „Јерусалимски“ and „Цариградски“ did earlier in this range. The bare forename is what is left. `foldchk.py` returns `pancratius-the-martyr-12-may`, `sr`, for «Панкратије», so this is the second folder on the string, and the heading offers no by-name to break it with — the city in it being a see and not a by-name.

hymns.text: Şi părtaş obiceiurilor şi următor scaunelor apostolilor fiind, lucrare ai aflat, de Dumnezeu insuflate, spre suirea privirii la cele înalte. Pentru aceasta, cuvântul adevărului drept învăţând şi cu credinţa răbdând până la sânge Sfinţite Mucenice Pangratie, roagă-te lui Hristos Dumnezeu să mântuiască sufletele noastre.

source.text: Doxologia — Troparul Sfântului Sfințit Mucenic Pangratie, Episcopul Taorminei, Glasul 4

english.text: Sharer of their ways and successor to the thrones of the apostles, thou didst find in action, O God-inspired one, a way of ascent to the vision of things on high. Therefore, rightly dividing the word of truth, thou didst contend for the faith unto blood, O Hieromartyr Pancratius: pray to Christ God that our souls be saved.

source.text: Православный церковный календарь, Сретенский монастырь (days.pravoslavie.ru), 9 февраля ст. ст. — «Сщмчч. Маркелла, еп. Сикелийского, Филагрия, еп. Кипрского, и Панкратия, еп. Тавроменийского (I).»

feast.note: Doxologia keeps him twice: its calendar prints him on 9 februarie and again on 9 iulie, and his own page's feast line gives «9 Iulie». One row per church is the schema, so the row is the day this folder was read from and the second day is recorded here. Read 24 September 2026.

source.text: Calendarul zilei, Doxologia (doxologia.ro), 9 februarie — «Sfântul Sfințit Mucenic Pangratie, Episcopul Tavromeniei»
saint.gr, το εορτολόγιο της 9ης Φεβρουαρίου — «Άγιοι Μάρκελλος επίσκοπος Σικελίας, Φιλάγριος επίσκοπος Κύπρου και Παγκράτιος επίσκοπος Ταυρομενίου»

attestations.note: The page closes with a second day: «Η μνήμη του Αγίου Παγκρατίου, επαναλαμβάνεται και την 9η Ιουλίου» — his memory is repeated on 9 July. One attestation row is one feast, so the row records the day read and the second day stands here as a note. The same day's calendar separately keeps a Russian Pancratius the recluse of the Kiev Caves, who is another man.

source.text: Православни подсетник (pravoslavno.rs), Охридски пролог за 22.07.2026 (9. јул ст. ст.) — „Свешт. муч. Панкратије еп. Тавроменијски“

attestations.note: The day’s first entry. The heading is quoted as the Prologue prints it, without a closing full stop, as every heading of this wave is. **FOUR CALENDARS AND TWO DAYS, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS THE MONTH AND NOT THE DAY.** This folder’s three venerated rows — russian, romanian and greek — all stand on the **9 February**, and this book keeps him on the **9 July**: the same day-number in a different month, which is neither a thirteen-day conversion nor a near miss. §4’s second-day note belongs on a row of the **same** church that is already `venerated`, and this folder’s `serbian` row was `undocumented`, so the row is written plainly on the day this book gives and **nothing of the other three is touched**; the two days stand side by side here, as they do on `alexander-the-sleepless` from 3 July and on the two monks of Almyris from 7 July. **The identification is not in doubt**: „еп. Тавроменијски“ is this folder’s own `office`, «Bishop of Tauromenium», and the body has the city Tauromen, the ordination by the apostle Peter in agreement with the apostle Paul, the breaking of the idols and the death by stones. **`dates` UNTOUCHED, AND WHAT THIS BOOK ADDS WOULD NOT HAVE CHANGED THEM.** The folder holds `floruit` 1 to 100, display «1st century», off saint.gr: «Έζησαν και οι τρεῖς κατά τον πρώτο μετά Χριστόν αιώνα». This book gives no year at all, and instead dates him by the strongest possible means and the one this corpus refuses to read as a date: he was born at Antioch „у време када Господ Исус хођаше као човек међу људима на земљи“, in the time when the Lord Jesus walked as a man among men on earth. That is a period and not a year, it agrees with the century already recorded, and **it is written into the life and into no field**. WHAT IS NEW, AND THE OPENING OF IT IS REMARKABLE. That his parents, hearing of Christ’s wonders, wished to see the Lord the wonderworker and came with Pancratius to Jerusalem, **where they saw Jesus, heard His words and saw His wonders** — and that it was there Pancratius came to know the apostle Peter. That after the Ascension both parents and son were baptised at Antioch. That he withdrew to a cave in Pontus, where Peter found him. **The siege, which is the whole second half of the entry**: a pagan commander Aquilinus, hearing that the whole city of Tauromen had become Christian, marched on it to destroy it; Pancratius encouraged the faithful not to fear and went out of the city with his clergy carrying „непобедиво оружје, крст часни“, the invincible weapon, the honourable cross; and as the army drew near **a darkness fell on it and a great fear took it**, and such confusion arose that the attackers turned on one another and stabbed and cut one another down with their swords. And the end: he was killed with stones by certain envious and malicious pagans, and **his holy relics rest at Rome**. `types` UNTOUCHED: `hieromartyr` and `bishop` are both there, „Свешт. муч.“ is the `hieromartyr` and „еп.“ the `bishop`. **`wonderworker` is refused**: „почини велика чудеса“ stands in the body. `office` UNTOUCHED at «Bishop of Tauromenium», which is what the heading says. No `locations`: Antioch, Jerusalem, Pontus, Tauromen and Rome in a narrative are not coordinates, and a folder dated to a whole century with a `locations` would have to answer `map-span`. **NO NEW ROWS, AND THE TWO APOSTLES ARE THE DAY’S NEAREST MISS.** The folder already relates `marcellus-of-sicily`, `philagrius-of-cyprus`, `aisia-disciple-of-pancratius` and `susanna-disciple-of-pancratius`, none of whom this book names. **Peter and Paul take no row.** Peter ordains him and finds him in the cave, and Paul agrees to it, which is as close to this man’s story as an apostle gets — and the rule is still that an identification made off a name in another man’s life is not an identification, and that a `related` row is a reading. The prose names them as the book does, «the apostle Peter» and «the apostle Paul», which are not the display names of `peter-the-apostle` or `paul-the-apostle`. Aquilinus is a persecutor; the darkness and the confusion are not folders. The Prologue prints no troparion and no kontakion; the day carries only the verse.

floruit.note: saint.gr, of the three bishops on the page together: «Έζησαν και οι τρεῖς κατά τον πρώτο μετά Χριστόν αιώνα». No year of birth or repose is given.
